metadata.description: Overrides the @nx/vitest-inferred target's `inputs`, which cover only this project's files. The API conventions tests (#506) read three files outside it: openapi-conventions.test.ts checks stable-surface/openapi.json and apps/docs-site/public/openapi.json, and problem.test.ts compares the code table of apps/docs-site/src/content/docs/reference/api-conventions.md with PROBLEM_CODES. The realm-by-host lint guard test (default-realm-rule.test.ts, #487) lints samples with blocks of `.oxlintrc.json`, so that file and Oxlint itself (and TypeScript, which reads the configuration's comments) are inputs too; the request-authority guard test (request-authority-rule.test.ts, #490) and the egress guard test (egress-rule.test.ts, #481) also load the local plugin that implements their rules, `tools/oxlint/qauth-plugin.mjs`. experimental-surface.test.ts (#477) generates apps/wire-suite/src/fixtures/experimental.ts from apps/docs-site/public/openapi.json and formats it with Oxfmt and `.oxfmtrc.json`, so the generated file, the formatter and its configuration are inputs as well. admin-permissions-page.test.ts (#507) generates apps/docs-site/src/content/docs/reference/admin-permissions.md from the admin permission registry the same way (`pnpm nx test auth-server -- -u` rewrites it), so that page is an input too, and admin-permissions-surface.test.ts compares apps/docs-site/public/schemas/admin-permissions.json, which `auth-server:admin-permissions-export` writes, with the registry and checks that stable-surface/surfaces.json registers it. admin-operations-page.test.ts (#508) generates apps/docs-site/src/content/docs/reference/security-operations.md from the admin operation registry in the same way. Without them a change to one of those files would replay a cached pass. Setting `inputs` replaces the inferred array, so the first six entries are the inferred defaults re-declared, with `oxlint`, `typescript` and `oxfmt` added to the external dependencies. account-contract.test.ts (#588) validates the account API contract against the official OpenAPI 3.1 schema with Ajv, hence `ajv` and `ajv-formats`; the contract itself is a dependency, so its changes are already inputs.

test-integration.description: Run the Docker-backed wallet-federation E2E suite (testcontainers Postgres + Redis). Requires a running Docker daemon.

metadata.description: Besides the shared `integration` inputs (nx.json), the admin-listener and egress-allowlist suites read the published OpenAPI documents stable-surface/openapi.json and apps/docs-site/public/openapi.json, and the account and developer API suite imports the developer portal's auth-server client from apps/developer-portal/src by path. CI selects this target by its inputs (#1044), so each is named here.

Declared here because @nx/js/typescript (Nx 24) infers no `typecheck` target for a project whose build already type-checks it, and it counts this @nx/esbuild build as one (no `skipTypeCheck`). Nx 23 inferred one, and CI's `nx affected -t lint typecheck test build` and `nx typecheck auth-server` keep running it. Same command shape and inputs as the targets the plugin infers for the libraries and wire-suite, including their compiler (`"compiler": "tsgo"` in nx.json, TypeScript 7 from @typescript/native-preview): tsconfig.app.json (the only project tsconfig.json references) checked without emitting. The @nx/esbuild build still type-checks with the typescript 6.0 package.

keys:create.description: Create one key for a realm, purpose and algorithm in the realm's encrypted key store (ADR-019 Decision 9, #485), for example an RS256 signing key for an OpenID Foundation run: `pnpm nx run auth-server:keys:create --purpose=token_signing --algorithm=RS256`. Run it on a host that holds the KEK, with the server's environment (DATABASE_URL, KEK or KEK_PATH, SIGNING_ALGORITHM_MODE, HYBRID_SIGNING_ENABLED, DEFAULT_REALM_NAME).

keys:rewrap.description: Rotate the KEK (ADR-019 Decision 9, #545): re-wrap every stored key's data key from the old KEK to the new one, then print the stored keys per kek_ref and whether KEK_PREVIOUS can be removed. `pnpm nx run auth-server:keys:rewrap --status` counts the keys per kek_ref; `--from=<old kek_ref>` re-wraps them. Run it on a host that holds both KEKs, with the server's environment (DATABASE_URL, the new KEK as KEK or KEK_PATH and the old one as KEK_PREVIOUS or KEK_PREVIOUS_PATH).

keys:retire.description: Retire a token-signing key at once because it may be compromised (ADR-019 Decision 9, #551): mark it and its hybrid partner compromised, drop them from the JWKS, deny their kids at every verifier, sign with a new key, revoke the realm's refresh token families and end its sessions used since the key began to sign. `pnpm nx run auth-server:keys:retire --kid=<kid> --yes`; `--realm=<name>` for a realm other than DEFAULT_REALM_NAME. Run it on a host that holds the KEK, with the server's environment (DATABASE_URL of a role that may write the keys, tokens, sessions and audit log, REDIS_*, KEK or KEK_PATH).

service-accounts.description: Create a service account for the admin API in the operator realm, list them, or disable or enable one (ADR-019 Decision 7, #522): `pnpm nx run auth-server:service-accounts -- create --name=ci --client-id=ci --jwks-uri=https://ci.example.com/jwks.json --grant=security-admin@*`. The account authenticates with private_key_jwt and a DPoP proof; no secret is made. Run it on a host that holds the database credentials, with DATABASE_URL of a role that may write users, OAuth clients, service accounts, admin grants and the admin audit log.

openapi-export.description: Boot the real app (no Postgres/Redis required, no listening port) twice: under default flags to write stable-surface/openapi.json and the family baselines in docs/api-baseline/, and under the maximal flag surface, with the admin listener, to write apps/docs-site/public/openapi.json and the family documents openapi-{admin,account,developer}.json beside it (#525)

api-baseline.description: Regenerate the stable surfaces of the default flags alone: stable-surface/openapi.json and the family baselines docs/api-baseline/openapi-{admin,account,developer}.json (#525). openapi-export writes these and the docs site's documents too; the stable-surface check compares the baselines with the last release

admin-permissions-export.description: Write apps/docs-site/public/schemas/admin-permissions.json, the admin permission catalog as a JSON Schema (#507), from the registry in src/app/helpers/admin-permissions.ts. The stable-surface check runs it, fails on drift, and reports a removed permission or a changed class as a break against the latest release.
